### Lines 673-684 / 第 673-684 行

```tablegen
 673:     The `nvvm.mbarrier.inval` operation invalidates an *mbarrier object* at the 
 674:     specified memory location. 
 675: 
 676:     This operation marks the *mbarrier object* as invalid, making it safe to repurpose 
 677:     the memory location for other uses or to reinitialize it as a new *mbarrier object*.
 678:     It is undefined behavior if the *mbarrier object* is already invalid.
 679:     
 680:     The operation takes the following operand:
 681:     - `addr`: A pointer to the memory location of the *mbarrier object*. The `addr`
 682:       must be a pointer to generic or shared::cta memory. When it is generic, the
 683:       underlying address must be within the shared::cta memory space; otherwise
 684:       the behavior is undefined.
```

### Lines 877-888 / 第 877-888 行

```tablegen
 877:     expect-tx operation increases the expect-count of the *mbarrier object* by the
 878:     specified value (i.e. `txcount`), setting the current phase to expect and track
 879:     the completion of additional asynchronous transactions.
 880: 
 881:     The operation takes the following operands:
 882:     - `addr`: A pointer to the memory location of the *mbarrier object*. Uses generic 
 883:       addressing, but the address must still be in the shared memory space.
 884:     - `txcount`: An unsigned integer specifying the expected transaction count 
 885:       for the expect-tx operation. This represents the number of asynchronous transactions 
 886:       expected to complete before the barrier phase completes.
 887:     - `scope`: This specifies the set of threads that directly observe the memory
 888:       synchronizing effect of the `mbarrier.test.wait` operation.
```

1033:       The `phase` is an integer specifying the phase parity (0 or 1).

1036:       synchronizing effect of the `mbarrier.test.wait` operation.
1037:     - `relaxed`: When set to true, the `arrive` operation has relaxed memory semantics
1038:       and does not provide any ordering or visibility guarantees.

```tablegen
1129:   let description = [{
1130:     The `nvvm.barrier` operation performs barrier synchronization and communication 
1131:     within a CTA (Cooperative Thread Array). It causes executing threads to wait for 
1132:     all non-exited threads participating in the barrier to arrive.
1133: 
1134:     The operation takes two optional operands:
1135:

```tablegen
1681:     The `nvvm.prmt` operation constructs a permutation of the
1682:     bytes of the first one or two operands, selecting based on 
1683:     the 2 least significant bits of the final operand.
1684:     
1685:     The bytes in the first one or two source operands are numbered. 
1686:     The first source operand (%lo) is numbered {b3, b2, b1, b0}, 
1687:     in the case of the '``default``', '``f4e``' and '``b4e``' variants, 
1688:     the second source operand (%hi) is numbered {b7, b6, b5, b4}.
1689: 
1690:     Modes:
1691:     - `default`: Index mode         - each nibble in `selector` selects a byte from the 8-byte pool
1692:     - `f4e`    : Forward 4 extract  - extracts 4 contiguous bytes starting from position in `selector`
```

1695:     - `ecl`    : Edge clamp left    - clamps out-of-range indices to the leftmost valid byte
1696:     - `ecr`    : Edge clamp right   - clamps out-of-range indices to the rightmost valid byte  
1697:     - `rc16`   : Replicate 16       - replicates the lower 16 bits across the 32-bit result
1698: 
1699:     Depending on the 2 least significant bits of the %selector operand, the result

1702:     +------------+----------------+--------------+

1704:     +------------+----------------+--------------+

```tablegen
3265: 
3266:     `b1Op` is only relevant when the binary (b1) type is given to
3267:     `multiplicandDataType`. It specifies how the multiply-and-acumulate is
3268:     performed and is either `xor_popc` or `and_poc`. The default is `xor_popc`.
3269: 
3270:     `intOverflowBehavior` is only relevant when the `multiplicandType` attribute
3271:     is one of `u8, s8, u4, s4`, this attribute describes how overflow is handled
3272:     in the accumulator. When the attribute is `satfinite`, the accumulator values
3273:     are clamped in the int32 range on overflow. This is the default behavior.
3274:     Alternatively, accumulator behavior `wrapped` can also be specified, in
3275:     which case overflow wraps from one end of the range to the other.

### Lines 3493-3504 / 第 3493-3504 行

```tablegen
3493:     `D = matmul(A_sparse, B) + C` using all threads in a warp.
3494: 
3495:     This operation is similar to `nvvm.mma.sync` but with structured sparsity
3496:     in the A operand. The sparsity follows the 2:4 structured sparse pattern
3497:     where 2 out of every 4 elements are non-zero.
3498: 
3499:     All the threads in the warp must execute the same `mma.sp.sync` operation.
3500: 
3501:     The `sparseMetadata` operand provides the sparsity indices that indicate
3502:     which elements in the A operand are non-zero. The `sparsitySelector`
3503:     controls how the indices are distributed among threads in the warp and
3504:     should typically be 0 or 1.
```

### Lines 3505-3516 / 第 3505-3516 行

```tablegen
3505: 
3506:     The optional `orderedMetadata` attribute specifies the metadata ordering:
3507:     - Absence (default): Uses standard sparse metadata ordering
3508:     - Presence: Uses ordered metadata (PTX ISA 8.5+, sm_90+)
3509: 
3510:     The optional `kind` attribute specifies mixed-precision modes for FP8 operations:
3511:     - `f8f6f4`: Enables e3m2, e2m3, e2m1 FP8 types and f16 accumulator (PTX ISA 8.7+, sm_90+)
3512:     - Only valid with ordered metadata and m16n8k64 shape
3513: 
3514:     The shapes, layouts, and data types follow the same constraints as the
3515:     regular `nvvm.mma.sync` operation, but the A operand contains only the
3516:     non-zero elements in compressed format.

### Lines 4045-4056 / 第 4045-4056 行

```tablegen
4045:     TMA Tensor Ops support the following modes, when copying data from
4046:     global memory to shared memory (i.e. load):
4047: 
4048:     Tile Mode: It's the default mode. The source multi-dimensional tensor
4049:     layout is preserved at the destination.
4050:     [For more information, see PTX ISA](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/parallel-thread-execution/#tensor-tiled-mode)
4051: 
4052:     Im2col Mode: This mode is used when `im2colOffsets` operands are present.
4053:     The elements in the Bounding Box of the source tensor are rearranged into
4054:     columns at the destination. In this mode, the tensor has to be at least
4055:     3-dimensional. The number of `im2colOffsets` is `dims - 2` where `dims`
4056:     is the dimension of the tensor.
```

4605:     access. The `byteMask` operand is optional. The i-th bit in the 16-bit
4606:     wide `byteMask` specifies whether the i-th byte of each 16-byte wide
4607:     chunk of source data is copied to the destination. If the bit is set,
4608:     the byte is copied.

### Lines 6145-6156 / 第 6145-6156 行

```tablegen
6145:     The `tcgen05.mma.block_scale` operation is an asynchronous tensor core instruction
6146:     that performs matrix multiplication, accumulation with block scaling in a
6147:     single fused operation. It targets 5th-generation tensor cores, providing
6148:     developers with fine-grained control over execution and scheduling.
6149: 
6150:     ```
6151:     D = (A * scale_a)  * (B * scale_b)`      // if `enableInputD` is false
6152:     D = (A * scale_a)  * (B * scale_b) + D`
6153:     ```
6154: 
6155:     where:
6156:     - A is an M x (K / 2) matrix in tensor memory or described using shared memory descriptor
```
